questions.scenario: A team on Java 21 wants to adopt new features. A colleague proposes using `StructuredTaskScope` from Java 25 in the payment service right away.
questions.question: What should you point out?
options: Nothing; every Java 25 feature is final
Structured concurrency is still a preview in Java 25: it needs `--enable-preview`, can change, and shouldn't go to production
It only works on platform threads
questions.explanation: Preview features are complete but not yet stable. Use final features (scoped values, gatherers, flexible constructor bodies) in production; experiment with previews elsewhere.

questions.scenario: A bulk-payment partner accepts at most 100 transfers per request. You have a `List<Transfer>` of 4,350 transfers on Java 25.
questions.question: Which is the clearest way to split them?
questions.explanation: `windowFixed(100)` emits consecutive lists of 100 (the last one smaller), with no index arithmetic to get wrong.

questions.scenario: On Java 21, a service using virtual threads stalls under load; JFR shows `jdk.VirtualThreadPinned` events inside a JDBC driver's `synchronized` methods.
questions.question: What does upgrading the runtime to Java 25 change?
options: Since Java 24 (JEP 491), virtual threads can unmount inside `synchronized`, so this pinning goes away without changing the driver
questions.explanation: Pinning on `synchronized` was the main practical limit of virtual threads in Java 21. Pinning in native code (JNI) still happens.

questions.scenario: A request ID is stored in a `ThreadLocal` so log lines deep in the call stack can include it. The team moves to Java 25 and one virtual thread per request.
questions.question: What does Java 25 offer that fits better?
options: A `ScopedValue` bound with `ScopedValue.where(REQUEST_ID, id).run(...)`: immutable, cleared when the scope ends, cheap with many virtual threads
questions.explanation: Scoped values (final in Java 25) share read-only context for a bounded scope, can't leak between requests, and are inherited by structured subtasks.

questions.scenario: A subclass constructor must reject a negative interest rate before calling `super(number)`. On Java 21 the team uses a static helper method inside the `super(...)` call.
questions.question: What does Java 25 allow instead?
options: Validation statements (that don't use `this`) before `super(...)`, thanks to flexible constructor bodies (JEP 513)
questions.explanation: Code before `super(...)` may check arguments and even assign the subclass's own fields, so an invalid object is never partly built.

questions.scenario: A team sets `<maven.compiler.release>25</maven.compiler.release>` and merges. CI passes, but production fails at startup with `UnsupportedClassVersionError`.
questions.question: What went wrong?
options: The production image still runs Java 21; class files compiled for 25 need a Java 25 runtime. Upgrade runtimes first, then raise the release level
questions.explanation: The compiler release level must not be higher than the oldest runtime that will run the code: CI agents, container images and servers.

questions.scenario: A memory-hungry service on Java 25 holds tens of millions of small objects. The team wants less heap use without code changes.
questions.question: Which option is designed for that?
options: `-XX:+UseCompactObjectHeaders`, which shrinks object headers from 12 to 8 bytes (opt-in in Java 25)
questions.explanation: Compact object headers became a product feature in Java 25 but are off by default. Measure heap and GC before and after enabling them.

questions.scenario: On Java 25, a file `Hello.java` contains only `void main() { IO.println("Hello"); }`.
questions.question: What happens with `java Hello.java`?
options: A compile error: no class is declared
It runs and prints Hello: compact source files and instance main methods are final in Java 25, and `java.lang.IO` provides `println`
It runs only inside Spring Boot
questions.explanation: JEP 512 made compact source files standard in Java 25, mainly for learning and small scripts. On Java 21 you still need a class and `public static void main(String[] args)`.
